correctness.rationale: The ring C[a,b,c,d,e,f]/(ab,bc,ca,de,ef,fd) is reduced with 9 minimal-prime polynomial plane quotients C[x,y], so its normalization is their product. Its diagonal image consists of polynomial families agreeing on common coordinate axes. Multiplying by each component idempotent proves a conductor element vanishes on both axes of every normalized plane, precisely giving cross products (ad,ae,af,bd,be,bf,cd,ce,cf); converse also follows from boundary compatibility. The quotient by this conductor is reduced union of six axes, normalized conductor restricts to (xy) on each plane, branch counts 1/3/9, and exact Hilbert-series subtraction 9/(1-t)^2-(1+2t)^2/(1-t)^2=(8+4t)/(1-t) gives defect multiplicity 12. Independent graded dimension calculation confirms degree0 8 and every positive degree12; this is a theorem for the affine germ, not a claim for its coarse moduli quotient.

value.rationale: The conductor and normalization defect are canonical invariants of a specific nine-branch deformation singularity: identify precise gluing along axes, how many branches collide, and a quantitative one-dimensional difference between germ and normalization. This precise information is useful for further algebraic deformation and moduli analysis, independent of the simple monomial nature of the proof.
